subject: Customer surge: throughput/latency spike — evidence & log handling
messages:
From: Emily Park <epark@bigretail.com>
To: support@redwood.com, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T08:43:00-07:00
Subject: Sudden throughput drop + 30% p95 latency spike — need logs

Hi team,

We experienced a sharp throughput degradation this morning around 08:10 PT. Token throughput dropped ~40% for our production route (model: redwood/gpt-13b-8k, pinned) and p95 latency jumped ~30%. Several customers reported timeouts. Attaching a small bundle of traces we pulled from our side.

Can you confirm what data/diagnostic logs you can share from your side? We need timestamp-aligned evidence for our incident review and vendor audit. Also want to confirm retention guarantees — this incident is part of our Q2 compliance audit.

Attachments: bigretail-client-traces-20270509.zip (attachments from BigRetail)

Thanks,
Emily Park
Sr. Platform Ops — BigRetail

---

From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@bigretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 30% p95 latency spike — need logs

Folks — Emily reached out with a production spike from BigRetail. Asking for what evidence we can provide during the incident window and how we handle retention/exports mid-incident. Marcus, can ops pull the runtime request logs, per-route token counts, and the serving node metrics for 07:50–08:30 PT? Lauren, loop in legal/sec if there are PII concerns. Jonas, can you prepare a short exec summary for their CTO (they may escalate) and the audit team.

I'll coordinate transfer method (S3 pre-signed vs. secure Sharepoint) — customer prefers a direct upload. We should keep copies in our internal retention store and note any redaction steps.

Mina
Mina Haddad
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

---

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@bigretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T10:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 30% p95 latency spike — need logs

Mina/Team — initial pull complete. Collected:
- Serving runtime request logs (route: /generate-bigretail-prod) 07:45–08:35 PT (gzip)
- Token accounting snapshots per minute for the route
- Node-level GPU util + host network metrics (60s samples) for impacted pool
- KV-cache hit/miss summary (high miss rate observed during peak)

I'm packaging into a timestamp-aligned tarball: performance-snapshot-20270509.tar.gz. No user-provided content appears to be present in payloads (these are request metadata and timings). Will keep raw logs in our internal incident S3 bucket (s3://redwood-incidents/BR-3491/20270509/) and provide a secure presigned link.

Question: per contract, do we send raw logs directly to the customer or redact request text and only provide metadata and aggregates? I recommend we provide: (1) redwood runtime logs (metadata + timestamps), (2) aggregated token metrics, (3) opaque request hashes — unless legal requests raw request content.

Marcus
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachment: performance-snapshot-20270509.tar.gz (runtime logs, metrics summary)

From: Emily Park <epark@bigretail.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T11:01:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 30% p95 latency spike — need logs

Thanks Marcus — for the audit we need as much alignment between our traces and yours as possible. We can consume metadata-only first but ultimately need request-level evidence for 10 sample requests that failed. We have DPA in place; request payloads are allowed to be shared under the data sharing addendum if transferred securely and logged.

Can you confirm: transfer method, retention window you intend to apply after handoff, and whether Redwood will mark these artifacts as "exported for customer audit" to avoid accidental deletion?

Emily

---

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@bigretail.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T12:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 30% p95 latency spike — need logs

Emily/Mina/Marcus — legal & security guidance below (summary):
1) Data scope: Under the DPA addendum we can share customer-specific request content for a limited set of samples, provided transfer uses our E2E encrypted artifact flow and we record the access in our audit logs.
2) Redaction: We will redact any fields containing 3rd-party PII not necessary for the incident. If BigRetail wants full request bodies, we need an explicit written request (email confirmation suffices) and must record the export as a controlled data extraction.
3) Retention & custody: Redwood will: (a) mark the exported bundle as "customer_evidence/BR-3491/20270509" in our retention system; (b) set retention freeze for 90 days from handoff to allow audit review; (c) record an export event in our audit log with the requester and purpose.
4) Transfer: propose pre-signed S3 link with KMS-encrypted bucket and one-time download token, or use the customer's secure Sharepoint. We will not send raw credentials over email.

Next steps: Mina to confirm export scope (metadata-only vs. sample full request bodies). Marcus to prepare redaction script and staged export. Jonas to write a one-page exec note for BigRetail CTO and our leadership.

Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

---

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <epark@bigretail.com>, Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-05-09T15:26:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput drop + 30% p95 latency spike — need logs

Emily — quick exec note and confirmation of next steps:

TL;DR: We observed an elevated KV-cache miss rate during 08:05–08:20 PT which correlates with the throughput drop and p95 latency increase. Marcus is staging runtime logs and token metrics. With your confirmation we will produce 10 sample request bodies you requested and deliver them via a KMS-encrypted presigned S3 export. Redwood will:
- Record an export event in our central audit log (ticket: JIRA-OPS-1284).
- Place the exported bundle in a retention freeze for 90 days and tag it as customer evidence (BR-3491).
- Provide a mapping file to align your trace IDs with our request IDs.

Please reply to confirm you want the 10 sample request bodies exported. Once we have the explicit confirmation we'll proceed within 2 hours and share the pre-signed download link and an MD5 checksum.

Thanks,
Jonas Weber
VP, Site Reliability
Redwood Inference
